1246287799298465792 [2020-04-04] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 56 🔁 2
Hot niche take:

Kegan's stages are universal only because everyone is universally afflicted with a dysfunction related to left hemisphere fixation.

In a culture where this wasn't so, there would still be developmental stages, but they'd be nearly unrecognizable as Kegan stages. https://t.co/5FTRWhWfQ8
  [Quoting @QiaochuYuan: @a_witch_in_time me and @Malcolm_Ocean are into this idea that mental health can't really institutionally acknowledge a "mental health condition" if *practically everyone has it*]
↓
1246287800472829952 [2020-04-04] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 16 🔁 1
The left hemisphere maintains a worldview that it thinks is consistent and perfect, always. That's its main job: to treat the world as something it understands and can manipulate. 

It denies the contradictions inherent to its map, whatever they are.
https://t.co/3MjoAyCiBn
  [Quoting @Malcolm_Ocean: Reality doesn't contradict itself.  ...that's your map.]
↓
1246287801500471297 [2020-04-04] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 20
The right hemisphere, by contrast, cares more about seeing things as they are than having a perfect model where all of the parts fit together and there's a right answer.

But we actively stunt this kind of thinking with modern culture & education.

https://t.co/wI2D4CWGmu
  [Quoting @Malcolm_Ocean: @jonnym1ller @buster @metalearn It wasn't until I was reading McGilchrist's book that I fully realized what a paradox *is*. 🤯  To left-hemisphere logic, it means "one or both of these propositions need to be rejected".  To right-hemisphere sense-making, it means "here's something I don't understand yet".]
↓
1246287802804862977 [2020-04-04] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 14
As people develop more sophisticated ways of making sense of the world, whether via rationality or new age stuff, they end up with some sort of system that they interpret everything through, stored in their left hemisphere.

This mostly runs their meaning-making show.
↓
1246287803677278208 [2020-04-04] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 18
Kegan 1 is before LH takes over
Kegan 2 is pre-ethical LH: I control the world to meet my needs
Kegan 3 subjects that to external ethical system
Kegan 4 learns to construct own internal system
Kegan 5 stops trying to do things with a single consistent system, so must be RH-based.
↓
1246287804763713536 [2020-04-04] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 14 🔁 1 [(SEED) type=quote_of_root]
My model clears up a common confusion with Kegan's model, which is "don't kids feel empathy? it clearly can't take until Kegan 3 to feel empathy."

Of course not. But if LH has taken over, it takes a bunch of development to hack together simulated empathy.

Images:
  - [Image #0] The image shows a text passage titled "INHERENT HEALING PROCESSES" that discusses how infants and children react to and recover from negative emotions like hurt, fear, and embarrassment.
    
    The passage is transcribed as follows:
    
    "INHERENT HEALING PROCESSES
    
    After being hurt, an infant will cry loudly and continuously and, if permitted to do so, will seem to recover from the hurt very quickly. After being frightened badly, an infant will scream and shake and perspire. After being angered, a yelling, vigorous tantrum will result, unless interfered with by others in the vicinity. rating.reasoning_summary: This strand traces the cultural suppression of emotional intelligence in boys, anchored by Malcolm Ocean's 2019 citation of Carol Gilligan's 'The Birth of Pleasure' (boys lose emotional capacity at ages 2-4, earlier than girls' puberty lockdown). The discourse is primarily *constructive* rather than dialectical—participants are validating a shared observation about childhood trauma and offering therapeutic frameworks (bio-emotive practice, co-counseling, Alice Miller's work). The boundary object is the claim that boys naturally possess high EQ which gets 'beaten out' by patriarchal conditioning. The arc moves from initial heartbreak (2019) through therapeutic practice (Qiaochu's crying threads, 2023) to contemporary debates about gender essentialism (2025). However, the strand lacks strong evolution—it's more a recurring *lament* than a refinement of the idea. The 2018 Rich Decibels thread on organizational decentralization and the 2025 gender debates are thematically related but don't build on the core Gilligan thesis. Utility is medium (therapeutic value for individuals) but the discourse doesn't produce new social technology or measurably shift community practice.

title: “Boys lose EQ at 2–4”: the thread that wouldn’t die
summary:
The line that kept detonating people was Malcolm Ocean relaying Carol Gilligan’s claim from *The Birth of Pleasure*: boys aged ~2–4 have “a fuckton of emotional intelligence” and then get it repressed so early “people think it doesn’t exist.” Qiaochu Yuan immediately calls it “the most heartbreaking thing i’ve ever heard,” and Visakanv piles on with “That was a gut punch”—the vibe is less “interesting psych theory” and more “oh, that explains a lifetime of numb men.”

From there it sprawls: Qiaochu posts book excerpts about fathers talking about their sons and suddenly hitting unnamed sadness—the “loss is audible,” like they can literally hear the difference between their adult voices and their sons’ voices “out there.” Earlier, Rich Decibels had already been yelling the organizational version of the same thesis: if you’re working with people raised as boys, you’ll have to “retrain the EQ… shamed and beaten out of them as kids,” and he ties it to “smash the patriarchy” / vulnerability as the price of psychological safety. In 2020, the thread briefly peaks into an actual dispute: GeniesLoki floats “treat being male as a learning disability,” then argues hormones matter (trans people as evidence); Malcolm concedes hormones are real but insists he’s talking pre-puberty trauma. Malcolm then tries to systematize it with a Kegan + McGilchrist move: empathy exists early, but once left-hemisphere “fixation” takes over, adults have to “hack together simulated empathy” via development.

By 2023 the energy shifts from diagnosis to “what do I do with my body?”: Qiaochu goes mega-viral claiming adults rarely let crying *complete*, that culture repeatedly shuts off emotional discharge, and that years of metaphysical despair can be… “needing to poop out of your mouth and eyes.” He points people to co-counseling / NEDERA-style bio-emotive practice and describes multiple “central heartbreak of my entire life” moments that dissolve into “huh. okay. now what.” The whole thing ends up looping back into reading lists (Alice Miller’s *Drama of the Gifted Child* gets passed around as the hyperempathy/reverse-parenting companion text) and then, in 2025, into soft counter-anecdotes: Ozy Frantz says their son cries easily, likes art, and doesn’t do pretend violence—poking at the “it’s universal male conditioning” certainty. Why care: because this one claim became a hub for how people explain men’s emotional flatness, workplace dysfunction, parenting dread, and a very practical question—whether healing is “better arguments about gender” or simply finally letting the body finish the cry it got trained to interrupt.
